title: Katsura: Ancient Katsura Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Worshipped as Fudo Myoo beside a Sapporo hot spring, and growing in Boston from seed a college president mailed home in 1878. Three katsuras mapped.
intro: Katsura grows wild in the old forests of Japan, and the trees mapped here show how far its reputation travels from there. On Sapporo's Maruyama hill, inside a national natural monument forest, one katsura reaches enormous size on the shaded north slope; at the hot spring in Koganeyu, a katsura became a god, worshipped as Fudo Myoo standing in tree form, with a torii and a straw rope in front of it. The Boston pair carries the species further still: grown from seed William S. Clark, the American college president who helped found Hokkaido University, collected in 1876 and sent to his friend Charles Sprague Sargent, the Arnold Arboretum's first director, arriving in 1878. A tree tied to fire and water in Japanese folklore now shades a meadow in Jamaica Plain because two men once traded seed packets across an ocean. Three mapped so far, in two countries.
